newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Semicon plans T$400 bln plants.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Semicon plans T$400 bln plants.

text.p: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp said on Thursday it would build six advanced wafer-fabrication plants as part of a T$400 billion investment at southern Taiwan's Tainan Science-based Industrial Park.
The planned facilities include a T$80 billion wafer fab to make 12-inch semiconductors and a T$40 billion fab to make 8-inch wafers, the company said in a statement.

The Tainan investment would be worth T$400 billion (US$14.5 billion) over 10 years, making it Taiwan's largest single industrial project -- bigger even than Formosa group's huge T$240 billion (US$9 billion) petrochemical plant at Yunlin.
The project gives a significant boost to the fledgling Tainan facility, a new southern rival to Taiwan's main high-technology manufacturing park in northern Hsinchu.
Taiwan Semiconductor president Donald Brooks said his firm was "moving energetically to bring its long-term investment plans in line with the national policy of developing southern Taiwan".
"The T$400 billion, 10-year TSIP Manufacturing Centre project has been carefully formulated and will be carried out step by step," Brooks said in the statement.

"Because of its efficient organisation, plentiful land and high-quality human resources, Tainan Science-based Industrial Park is the best possible location for (Taiwan Semiconductor) to expand its manufacturing facilities," Brooks added.
The cluster of wafer fabs and research and development facilities would employ 5,000 people -- more than doubling the firm's current 4,300-strong workforce.

Taiwan's top chipmaker operates two six-inch wafer fabs and two eight-inch wafer fabs in Taiwan. A third eight-inch fab is under construction in Taiwan and a fourth in the United States through a joint venture, it said.

Taiwan Semiconductor said it expected the global microchip market to grow to US$300 billion by 2000, with demand soaring for chip-based three-dimensional multimedia, ISDN, high-speed modems, digital video, digital television equipment and digital telephones, mobile phones and cameras.

Taiwan Semiconductor said on Wednesday its March sales fell a year-on-year 26.4 percent to T$2.797 billion, but said figure reflected a 23 percent rise compared with February's T$2.274 billion -- breaking a string of eight month-to-month declines dating to its monthly peak of T$3.801 billion in March 1996.
The company has forecast 1997 sales at T$35.22 billion.
